analysis: The length identity |G| = B(n) - sum_{i>=2} (i-1) MC_i holds for every greedy game n < 1500 and for 1500 uniformly random games; the split phase ends at the lazy Fibonacci representation for every n < 5000, and 300 random firing orders never change its end point or its length; the insertion hypothesis H-C19-4 fails for 288 of the first 300 n (first at n = 3).
assumptions: random games choose uniformly among legal moves (seeded)

hypothesis: H-C19-A (derived from a potential): length = B(n) - W for every game. H-C19-B: splits and combine-1s, applied in any order, end at the lazy Fibonacci representation of n after the same number of moves. H-C19-4 (bold): L(n+1) = L(n) + lambda(n), lambda(n) the longest game from the Zeckendorf representation of n plus one extra 1.
methodology: Greedy games for n < 1500 and 1500 random games (n <= 200): compare length with B(n) - W. Split phase (lowest-first) for n < 5000 against the lazy digits; 300 random firing orders (n <= 600). Exact longest games from Zeck(m) + [1] for m < 300.
question: Is the length of EVERY game equal to B(n) - sum_{i>=2} (i-1) MC_i (B = Cusenza's bound)? Where does the split phase of the greedy game end? Is L(n+1) = L(n) + (longest game from Zeck(n) + 1)?
